newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds trade weaker ahead of budget speech.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds trade weaker ahead of budget speech.

text.p: Canadian bonds traded weaker ahead of the release of the federal budget on Tuesday, with spreads to U.S. Treasuries widening, as some investors took profits on recent spread-narrowing trades, analysts said.

"The spreads have worked for them. Rather than waiting for the budget to come out and taking a chance some profit taking occurred. That's putting some pressure on us," said David Yu, a bond portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc.
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.53 to C$113.87 to yield 6.853 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 6/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 31 basis points from 28 basis points at Monday's close.
Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin presents the budget for fiscal 1997/98 at 1630 EST/2130 GMT. While eagerly anticipated, the budget is not expected to hold much surprise for financial markets.

"My personal feeling is that the market is behaving quite well. We've been seeing foreign buyers of Canada overseas the last few nights and I expect it to continue," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.48 to C$105.87 to yield 6.189 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.28 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to nine percent from 15 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.89 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.12 percent.
